clip_texts: SC-11 Person directing traffic
A police officer, flagger or first responder directs traffic at a junction or a scene

One concrete scenario (seeded sample of the logical
scenario)
ODD-20 Ego speed: 20.3 km/h (range 0 to 48 km/h)
ODD-19 Traffic direction by people: directing
ODD-04 Junctions: signalised
ODD-12 Illumination: night

Ego slows at 3 m/s², the firm level of FSR-03.02 (DQ-019, DQ-033);
choreography, not Autoware's planned braking
Safety goals at stake

SG-06 (ASIL D): Do not enter an intersection, roundabout or
crosswalk against right of way
MON-02 Map–world divergence
Pass criterion

The vehicle detects the person directing traffic, stops safely and
asks for remote assistance; it does not move on the signal alone,
and responders can stop or hold it (MON-02, FSR-07.05, FSR-06.01,
FSR-02.02, FM-16, HR-08, AC-02)
Autoware's planned path (EL-01 Autoware computer, rated QM)
Safety monitor's envelope (EL-02, ASIL D); length not computed: the vehicle is not chosen yet (DQ-008)
Meant to do: stops, does not move on the signal
Dashed green: the path the pass criterion asks of the vehicle; green ring: where it is judged
Where the hazard lies: Person directing traffic
Amber, ringed: the road user the scenario is about
